original.target_description: Located Study 2, initial unadjusted across-participants comparison of moral judgments for direct versus indirect harm over eight scenarios: direct option judged more immoral 26.2% versus indirect 9.5%, t53 = 5.12, one-tailed. This matches the supplied PDF-page locator 9–11 and neutral moral-judgment description but conflicts with supplied study_o = 1.

n.sample_role: Participants completing the Study 2 web questionnaire, contributing eight within-participant scenario judgments each to the initial across-participants t test (df 53); not 432 independent participants.
n.exclusions: No participant exclusions reported for this initial test. The later directness-agreement restriction and discounted-response analysis are separate tests and are not combined with this estimate.
n.location: Typeset article/proof, printed p. 171 (PDF p. 7), Study 2 Method; printed p. 173 (PDF p. 9), initial Results and Discussion paragraph and 8 × 54 observations description.
n.quote:
Fifty-four subjects (ages 17–69, median age 34, 22% students, 69% females)
               completed a questionnaire on the World Wide Web for $3.

es.location: Typeset article/proof, printed p. 173 (PDF p. 9), Study 2 Results and Discussion, first paragraph; initial across-subjects comparison.

p.location: Typeset article/proof, printed p. 173 (PDF p. 9), Study 2 Results and Discussion, first paragraph; initial across-subjects t53 = 5.12, one-tailed.

notes: Fresh original-only validation. Source retained as complete typeset article/proof, with production headers/crop marks; not silently relabelled final press version. Title/authors and printed 2002 date visually checked on PDF p. 1. Rendered PDF pp. 5, 7, 9 and 10 checked for study identity and numeric meanings. Locator conflict: study_o identifies Study 1, but PDF pp. 9–10 report Study 2 and PDF p. 11 starts Study 3. The located initial Study 2 moral-judgment test is recorded with target_match false rather than treated as a confirmed Study 1 result. Study 1 is on printed pp. 168–170 (PDF pp. 4–6); its p. 169 reports 176 total participants, scenario-specific samples, and a binomial p < 0.001 for each scenario, with no single printed binomial test statistic identifying a unique target. No Study 1 sample/test was merged into Study 2. Study 2 also prints an across-scenarios test t7 = 3.47, p = 0.0052, and a later restricted/discounted analysis t50 = 3.24, p = .0011; these are distinct tests and were not substituted. The selected p is retained exactly as printed (rounded 0.0000, not interpreted as mathematical zero). Canonical text flattens the visually subscripted df into t53; the preserved quote includes the canonical line break before 5.12. No numeric discrepancy between canonical text and rendered target page was found. Unassigned replication and reported_success remain null placeholders.
